record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: What new nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics arise on graphs when one changes the vertex boundary conditions away from the standard cases studied here? In particular, can different vertex couplings produce new branches of standing waves, bifurcations of ground states, or symmetry-breaking phenomena analogous to those known for the line with a δ′ interaction?

evidence.quote: A different extension could be in the direction of different boundary conditions at the vertices. In such a case one expects new dynamical effects, for example bifurcation and symmetry breaking of ground states as proved for the NLS on the line with δ′ interaction (see[49]).

artifact.category_tag: NLS on metric graphs with vertex couplings
artifact.status_search_result: Several works since 2014 have addressed pieces of this program. Bifurcations and stability of standing waves on the tadpole graph with Kirchhoff conditions were analyzed (Noja-Pelinovsky-Shaikhova, 2014). More recently, NLS on looping-edge graphs with δ′-type vertex interactions has been studied, establishing existence and (in)stability of standing waves with explicit bifurcation/symmetry-breaking results (arXiv:2601.00158, arXiv:2507.10821), and symmetry-breaking on star graphs with inhomogeneities has been investigated (arXiv:2509.02145). However, a complete classification covering general graphs and general self-adjoint vertex couplings remains open.
